Validation schemas
==================

.. currentmodule:: streamlink.plugin.api.validate

Introduction
------------

The :ref:`streamlink.plugin.api.validate <api/validate:Validation schemas>` module provides an API for defining declarative
validation schemas which are used to verify and extract data from various inputs, for example HTTP responses.

Validation schemas are a powerful tool for :ref:`plugin <api/plugin:Plugin>` implementors to find and extract data like
stream URLs, stream metadata and more from websites and web APIs.

$ streamlink --output "~/recordings/{author}/{category}/{id}-{time:%Y%m%d%H%M%S}.ts" <URL> [STREAM]

The :option:`--json` argument always lists the conditional metadata.

.. code-block:: console

    $ streamlink --json twitch.tv/bobross | jq .metadata

.. code-block:: json

    {
      "id": "49163597677",
      "author": "BobRoss",
      "category": "Art",
      "title": "A Happy Little Weekend Marathon!"
    }

.. note::

    Streamlink is not designed as a tool for general-purpose metadata retrieval. If your goal is to extract metadata from
    specific streaming sites, then it's usually a better idea to implement this metadata retrieval yourself using
    the available APIs of those sites or other means.

Instead of verifying and extracting data programatically and having to perform error handling manually,
declarative validation schemas allow defining comprehensive validation and extraction rules which are easy to understand
and which raise errors with meaningful messages upon extraction failure.

.. admonition:: Public interface
   :class: caution

   While the internals are implemented in the ``streamlink.validate`` package,
   :ref:`streamlink.plugin.api.validate <api/validate:Validation schemas>` provides the main public interface
   for plugin implementors.


Examples
--------

Simple schemas
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Let's begin with a few simple validation schemas which are not particularly useful yet.

.. code-block:: pycon

"""
$description Russian live-streaming and video hosting social platform.
$url ok.ru
$url mobile.ok.ru
$type live, vod
$metadata id
$metadata author
$metadata title
"""

import logging
import re
from urllib.parse import unquote

from streamlink.exceptions import NoStreamsError
from streamlink.plugin import Plugin, pluginmatcher
from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
from streamlink.stream.dash import DASHStream
from streamlink.stream.hls import HLSStream
from streamlink.stream.http import HTTPStream


log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@pluginmatcher(
    name="default",
    pattern=re.compile(r"https?://(?:www\.)?ok\.ru/"),
)
@pluginmatcher(
    name="mobile",
    pattern=re.compile(r"https?://m(?:obile)?\.ok\.ru/"),
)
class OKru(Plugin):
    QUALITY_WEIGHTS = {
        "full": 1080,
        "1080": 1080,
        "hd": 720,
        "720": 720,
        "sd": 480,
        "480": 480,
        "360": 360,
        "low": 360,
        "lowest": 240,
        "mobile": 144,
    }

    @classmethod
    def stream_weight(cls, key):
        weight = cls.QUALITY_WEIGHTS.get(key)
        if weight:
            return weight, "okru"

        return super().stream_weight(key)

    def _canonicalize_mobile_url(self):
        url = self.session.http.get(
            self.url,
            schema=validate.Schema(
                validate.parse_html(),
                validate.xml_xpath_string(".//head/link[@rel='canonical'][@href][1]/@href"),
                validate.none_or_all(
                    validate.url(),
                ),
            ),
        )
        if not url or not self.matchers["default"].pattern.match(url):
            raise NoStreamsError

        self.url = url

>>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> schema_one = validate.Schema("123")
    >>> schema_two = validate.Schema(123)
    >>> schema_three = validate.Schema(int, 123.0)

    >>> schema_one.validate("123")
    '123'
    >>> schema_two.validate(123)
    123
    >>> schema_three.validate(123)
    123

First, three :class:`Schema` instances are created, ``schema_one``, ``schema_two`` and ``schema_three``.

The :class:`Schema` class is the main schema validation interface and the outer wrapper for all schema definitions.
It is a subclass of :class:`validate.all <all>` which additionally implements the :meth:`Schema.validate()` method.
This interface is expected by various Streamlink methods and functions when passing the ``schema`` argument/keyword,
for example to the :class:`HTTPSession <streamlink.session.Streamlink.http>` methods or :mod:`streamlink.utils.parse` functions.

The :class:`validate.all <all>` class takes a sequence of schema object arguments and validates each one in order.
All schema objects in this schema container must be valid.

Schema objects can be anything, and depending on their type, different validations will be applied. In our example, both
``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``"123"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas
``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate
only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.

As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't
much interesting in this example.

The ``"123"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for
all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,
and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object
and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.
``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.
This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected
when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,
the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole
``schema_three`` to be ``123``.

Now let's have a look at validation errors.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> schema_one.validate(123)
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):
      123 does not equal '123'

    >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):
      Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float

The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``"123"``, so
a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>` is raised because the input value is not equal to
the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in
a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.

The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for
the type ``int``, and despite the following schema being ``123.0``, which is a ``float`` object that would obviously validate
a ``123.0`` ``float`` input when comparing equality, a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`
is raised.

Extracting JSON data

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The next example shows how to read an optional integer value from JSON data.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> json_schema = validate.Schema(
    ...     str,
    ...     validate.parse_json(),
    ...     {
    ...         "status": validate.any(None, int),
    ...     },
    ...     validate.get("status"),
    ... )

    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":null}""")
    None
    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":123}""")
    123

    >>> json_schema.validate("""Not JSON""")
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError:
      Unable to parse JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ('Not JSON')

    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":"unknown"}""")
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(dict):
      Unable to validate value of key 'status'
      Context(AnySchema):
        ValidationError(equality):
          'unknown' does not equal None
        ValidationError(type):
          Type of 'unknown' should be int, but is str

Once again, we start with a new :class:`Schema` object which gets assigned to ``json_schema``. This schema collection validates
four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.

Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set
``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.

Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns
a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns
something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input
is indeed valid JSON data.

Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema
be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which
must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.
For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is
a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.

Here, the ``"status"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to
:class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.
Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema
that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be
``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.

If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated
by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.

The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.
This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.
And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``"status"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.
The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using
the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` schemas, but this isn't relevant here.

Finding stream URLs in HTML
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Let's imagine a simple website where a stream URL is embedded as JSON data in a ``data-player`` attribute of an unknown
HTML element where the web player of that website reads from.

Extracting this data could be done by using regular expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,
as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing
a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.

Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query
for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.

We also don't want to raise validation errors unnecessarily when the user inputs a URL where no video player was found,
so we can instead return an empty list of streams in our plugin implementation and let Streamlink's CLI exit gracefully.
Validation errors are only supposed to be raised when an actual error happened due to unexpected data,
not when streams are offline or inaccessible.

Thanks to validation schemas, we can do all this declaratively without causing a mess when doing this programmatically.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> schema = validate.Schema(
    ...     validate.parse_html(),
    ...     validate.xml_xpath_string(".//*[@data-player][1]/@data-player"),
    ...     validate.none_or_all(
    ...         validate.parse_json(),
    ...         {
    ...             validate.optional("url"): validate.url(
    ...                 path=validate.endswith(".m3u8"),
    ...             ),

...         },
    ...         validate.get("url"),
    ...     ),
    ... )

    >>> schema.validate("""
    ...     <!doctype html>
    ...     <section class="no-video-player"></section>
    ... """)
    None

    >>> schema.validate("""
    ...     <!doctype html>
    ...     <section
    ...         class="video-player"
    ...         data-player="{
    ...             "title":"Offline"
    ...         }"
    ...     >
    ...         ...
    ...     </section>
    ... """)
    None

    >>> schema.validate("""
    ...     <!doctype html>
    ...     <section
    ...         class="video-player"
    ...         data-player="{
    ...             "title":"Live",
    ...             "url":"https://host/hls-playlist.m3u8"
    ...         }"
    ...     >
    ...         ...
    ...     </section>
    ... """)
    'https://host/hls-playlist.m3u8'

    >>> schema.validate("""
    ...     <!doctype html>
    ...     <section
    ...         class="video-player"
    ...         data-player="{
    ...             "title":"Live",
    ...             "url":"https://host/dash-manifest.mpd"
    ...         }"
    ...     >
    ...         ...
    ...     </section>
    ... """)
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(NoneOrAllSchema):
      ValidationError(dict):
        Unable to validate value of key 'url'
        Context(url):
          Unable to validate URL attribute 'path'
          Context(endswith):
            '/dash-manifest.mpd' does not end with '.m3u8'

We start with a new :class:`Schema` and begin by parsing HTML using the :func:`validate.parse_html() <parse_html>`
utility function. Similar to :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>`, it returns a :class:`validate.transform <transform>`
schema. :func:`validate.parse_html() <parse_html>` however returns a parsed HTML node tree via Streamlink's
:ref:`lxml dependency <install:Dependencies>`.

This is followed by an XPath query schema using the :func:`validate.xml_xpath_string() <xml_xpath_string>` utility function.
:func:`validate.xml_xpath_string() <xml_xpath_string>` is a wrapper for :func:`validate.xml_xpath() <xml_xpath>` which always
returns a string or ``None``, depending on the query result. This is useful for querying text contents or single attribute
values, like in this case. XPath queries on their own always return a result set, i.e. possibly multiple values, so when
trying to find single values, it is important to limit the number of potential return values to only one in the XPath query.

The query here attempts to find any node with a ``data-player`` attribute. It then limits the result set to the first found
element and then reads the value of its ``data-player`` attribute. :func:`validate.xml_xpath_string() <xml_xpath_string>`
turns this into a single string return value, or ``None`` if no or an empty value was returned by the query.

Since we now have two different paths for our overall validation schema, either no player data or still unvalidated player data,
our next schema is a :class:`validate.none_or_all <none_or_all>` schema. This works similar to :class:`validate.all <all>`,
except that ``None`` inputs are skipped and get returned immediately without validating any sub-schemas. This lets us handle
cases where no player was found on the website, without raising
a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`.

In the :class:`validate.none_or_all <none_or_all>` schema, we now attempt to parse JSON data, which was already shown
previously, except for the fact that we don't need to validate the ``str`` input here, as the XPath query must have already
returned a string value.

On to the :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. We're only interested in the ``url`` key. Any other keys of the input
will get ignored. Since we're aware that ``url`` can be missing if the stream is offline, we mark it as optional using the
:class:`validate.optional <optional>` schema. This makes the :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>` not raise an error
if it's missing, but if it's set, then its value must validate. Talking about the value, we want its value to be a URL.

This is where the :func:`validate.url <url>` utility function comes in handy. It parses the input and lets us validate
any parts of the parsed URL with further validation schemas. The return value is always the full URL string. In our example,
we want to ensure that the URL's path ends with the ``".m3u8"`` string, which is an indicator for the stream being
an HLS stream, so we can pass the URL to Streamlink's :class:`HLS implementation <streamlink.stream.HLSStream>`.

Lastly, we simply get the ``url`` key using :class:`validate.get <get>`. The return value must either be ``None`` if no ``url``
key was included in the JSON data, or a ``str`` with a URL where its path ends with ``".m3u8"``.

This means that the overall schema can only return ``None`` or said kind of URL string. If the ``url`` key is not a URL,
or if its path does not end with ``".m3u8"``, then a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`
is raised, which is what we want. The ``None`` return value should then be checked accordingly by the plugin implementation.

This means that the first two schemas validate","L63: only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.","L64: ","L65: As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't","L66: much interesting in this example.","L67: ","L68: The ``\"123\"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for","L69: all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,","L70: and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object","L71: and then also returns the input value again. 要回答这个问题，我需要理解 streamlink 中流获取方法如何实现多阶段验证模式组合以提取和处理嵌入的媒体交付平台元数据。

从已提供的源码中，我可以看到：

1. **okru.py** 中的 `_get_streams` 方法展示了多阶段验证模式组合的典型实现：
   - 首先从 HTML 中提取 `data-options` 属性
   - 解析 JSON
   - 定义了一个 `schema_metadata` 来验证和提取元数据
   - 使用 `validate.parse_html()`、`validate.parse_json()` 等组合操作
   - 使用 `validate.union_get()` 提取多个字段

2. **cinergroup.py** 中的 `_schema_data_ht` 展示了类似的模式：
   - 使用 `validate.xml_xpath_string()` 定位元素
   - 使用 `validate.none_or_all()` 处理可选字段
   - 使用 `validate.parse_json()` 解析 JSON

3. **youtube.py** 中的 `_schema_streamingdata` 展示了更复杂的嵌套模式：
   - 处理嵌套的 `streamingData` 对象
   - 使用 `validate.regex()` 解析 MIME 类型
   - 使用 `validate.union_get()` 提取多个字段

4. **validate.rst** 文档说明了验证模式的基本概念：
   - 声明式验证模式用于验证和提取数据
   - 提供有意义的错误消息

In our example, both","L61: ``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``\"123\"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas","L62: ``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate","L63: only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.","L64: ","L65: As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't","L66: much interesting in this example.","L67: ","L68: The ``\"123\"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for","L69: all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,","L70: and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object","L71: and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.","L72: ``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.","L73: This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected","L74: when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,","L75: the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole","L76: ``schema_three`` to be ``123``.","L77: ","L78: Now let's have a look at validation errors.","L79: ","L80: .. code-block:: pycon","L81: ","L82:     >>> schema_one.validate(123)","L83:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):","L84:       123 does not equal '123'","L85: ","L86:     >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)","L87:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):","L88:       Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float","L89: ","L90: The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``\"123\"``, so","L91: a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>` is raised because the input value is not equal to","L92: the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in","L93: a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.","L94: ","L95: The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for","L96: the type ``int``, and despite the following schema being ``123.0``, which is a ``float`` object that would obviously validate","L97: a ``123.0`` ``float`` input when comparing equality, a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`","L98: is raised.","L99: ","L100: Extracting JSON data"]}],"next_line":null,"truncated":false,"unit":null,"requested_end_line":100,"requested_range":{"start_line":1,"end_line":100},"uncovered_ranges":[],"schema_version":"repomentor.tool.sources.v3","continuation":null}

This schema collection validates","L137: four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.","L138: ","L139: Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set","L140: ``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.","L141: ","L142: Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns","L143: a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns","L144: something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input","L145: is indeed valid JSON data.","L146: ","L147: Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema","L148: be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which","L149: must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.","L150: For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is","L151: a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.","L152: ","L153: Here, the ``\"status\"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to","L154: :class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.","L155: Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema","L156: that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be","L157: ``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.","L158: ","L159: If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated","L160: by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.","L161: ","L162: The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.","L163: This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.","L164: And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``\"status\"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.","L165: The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using","L166: the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,","L175: as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing","L176: a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.","L177: ","L178: Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query","L179: for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.","L180: ","L181: We also In our example, both","L61: ``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``\"123\"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas","L62: ``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate","L63: only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.","L64: ","L65: As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't","L66: much interesting in this example.","L67: ","L68: The ``\"123\"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for","L69: all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,","L70: and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object","L71: and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.","L72: ``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.","L73: This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected","L74: when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,","L75: the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole","L76: ``schema_three`` to be ``123``.","L77: ","L78: Now let's have a look at validation errors.","L79: ","L80: .. code-block:: pycon","L81: ","L82:     >>> schema_one.validate(123)","L83:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):","L84:       123 does not equal '123'","L85: ","L86:     >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)","L87:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):","L88:       Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float","L89: ","L90: The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``\"123\"``, so","L91: a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>` is raised because the input value is not equal to","L92: the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in","L93: a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.","L94: ","L95: The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for","L96: the type ``int``, and despite the following schema being ``123.0``, which is a ``float`` object that would obviously validate","L97: a ``123.0`` ``float`` input when comparing equality, a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`","L98: is raised.","L99: ","L100: Extracting JSON data"]}],"next_line":null,"truncated":false,"unit":null,"requested_end_line":100,"requested_range":{"start_line":1,"end_line":100},"uncovered_ranges":[],"schema_version":"repomentor.tool.sources.v3","continuation":null}

{"status":"ok","error_code":null,"spans":[{"path":"docs/api_guide/validate.rst","start_line":101,"end_line":200,"content_sha256":"e137c492895d3c8971905e2bf687ae8837a435aac0036f88b959a1880dddf103","lines":["L101: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^","L102: ","L103: The next example shows how to read an optional integer value from JSON data.","L104: ","L105: .. code-block:: pycon","L106: ","L107:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate","L108: ","L109:     >>> json_schema = validate.Schema(","L110:     ...     str,","L111:     ...     validate.parse_json(),","L112:     ...     {","L113:     ...         \"status\": validate.any(None, int),","L114:     ...     },","L115:     ...     validate.get(\"status\"),","L116:     ... )","L117: ","L118:     >>> json_schema.validate(\"\"\"{\"status\":null}\"\"\")","L119:     None","L120:     >>> json_schema.validate(\"\"\"{\"status\":123}\"\"\")","L121:     123","L122: ","L123:     >>> json_schema.validate(\"\"\"Not JSON\"\"\")","L124:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError:","L125:       Unable to parse JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ('Not JSON')","L126: ","L127:     >>> json_schema.validate(\"\"\"{\"status\":\"unknown\"}\"\"\")","L128:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(dict):","L129:       Unable to validate value of key 'status'","L130:       Context(AnySchema):","L131:         ValidationError(equality):","L132:           'unknown' does not equal None","L133:         ValidationError(type):","L134:           Type of 'unknown' should be int, but is str","L135: ","L136: Once again, we start with a new :class:`Schema` object which gets assigned to ``json_schema``. This schema collection validates","L137: four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.","L138: ","L139: Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set","L140: ``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.","L141: ","L142: Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns","L143: a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns","L144: something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input","L145: is indeed valid JSON data.","L146: ","L147: Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema","L148: be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which","L149: must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.","L150: For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is","L151: a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.","L152: ","L153: Here, the ``\"status\"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to","L154: :class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.","L155: Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema","L156: that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be","L157: ``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.","L158: ","L159: If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated","L160: by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.","L161: ","L162: The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.","L163: This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.","L164: And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``\"status\"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.","L165: The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using","L166: the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` schemas, but this isn't relevant here.","L167: ","L168: Finding stream URLs in HTML","L169: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^","L170: ","L171: Let's imagine a simple website where a stream URL is embedded as JSON data in a ``data-player`` attribute of an unknown","L172: HTML element where the web player of that website reads from.","L173: ","L174: Extracting this data could be done by using regular expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,","L175: as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing","L176: a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.","L177: ","L178: Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query","L179: for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.","L180: ","L181: We also don't want to raise validation errors unnecessarily when the user inputs a URL where no video player was found,","L182: so we can instead return an empty list of streams in our plugin implementation and let Streamlink's CLI exit gracefully.","L183: Validation errors are only supposed to be raised when an actual error happened due to unexpected data,","L184: not when streams are offline or inaccessible.","L185: ","L186: Thanks to validation schemas, we can do all this declaratively without causing a mess when doing this programmatically.","L187: ","L188: .. code-block:: pycon","L189: ","L190:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate","L191: ","L192:     >>> schema = validate.Schema(","L193:     ...     validate.parse_html(),","L194:     ...     validate.xml_xpath_string(\".//*[@data-player][1]/@data-player\"),","L195:     ...     validate.none_or_all(","L196:     ...         validate.parse_json(),","L197:     ...         {","L198:     ... Similar to :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>`, it returns a :class:`validate.transform <transform>`","L261: schema. :func:`validate.parse_html() <parse_html>` however returns a parsed HTML node tree via Streamlink's","L262: :ref:`lxml dependency <install:Dependencies>`.","L263: ","L264: This is followed by an XPath query schema using the :func:`validate.xml_xpath_string() <xml_xpath_string>` utility function.","L265: :func:`validate.xml_xpath_string() <xml_xpath_string>` is a wrapper for :func:`validate.xml_xpath() <xml_xpath>` which always","L266: returns a string or ``None``, depending on the query result. This is useful for querying text contents or single attribute","L267: values, like in this case. XPath queries on their own always return a result set, i.e. possibly multiple values, so when","L268: trying to find single values, it is important to limit the number of potential return values to only one in the XPath query.","L269: ","L270: The query here attempts to find any node with a ``data-player`` attribute. This makes the :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>` not raise an error","L287: if it's missing, but if it's set, then its value must validate. Streamlink 的流获取方法通过 **声明式验证模式组合（declarative validation schema composition）** 实现多阶段验证，以提取和处理嵌入的媒体交付平台元数据。其核心机制如下：

### 1. **多阶段验证管道**
验证模式按顺序组合成管道，每个阶段对前一阶段的输出进行验证和提取：
- **输入类型验证**：如 `str` 确保输入是字符串

- **结构验证**：如 `dict` 验证 JSON 对象结构
- **字段验证与提取**：如 `validate.get("key")` 提取特定字段

### 2. **组合操作符**
- **`validate.all()`**：按顺序验证多个 schema，每个 schema 的输出作为下一个 schema 的输入
- **`validate.any()`**：尝试多个 schema，返回第一个成功的结果
- **`validate.optional()`**：使字段验证可选，缺失时不报错
- **`validate.none_or_all()`**：如果输入为 `None` 则跳过验证，否则按 schema 验证
- **`validate.get()`**：从 dict 中提取指定键的值
- **`validate.union_get()`**：从 dict 中提取多个键的值

```python
schema_metadata = validate.Schema(
    validate.parse_html(),                    # 阶段 1: 解析 HTML
    validate.xml_find(".//*[@data-options]"), # 阶段 2: XPath 定位元素
    validate.get("data-options"),             # 阶段 3: 获取属性值
    validate.parse_json(),                    # 阶段 4: 解析 JSON

        ),
        "movie": validate.all(
            {...},                             # 验证 movie 结构
            validate.union_get("id", "title") # 提取 id 和 title
        ),
        "hlsManifestUrl": validate.url(),     # 验证 HLS URL
        "videos": [...],                      # 验证视频列表
    },
)
```

- 验证失败时抛出 `ValidationError`，包装在 `PluginError` 中
- 使用 `validate.optional()` 和 `validate.none_or_all()` 处理可选字段
- 错误消息包含验证失败的具体位置和原因

- **声明式而非程序式**：避免手动错误处理
- **管道式处理**：数据流经多个验证阶段
- **类型安全**：每个阶段验证特定类型

## 答案

Streamlink 的流获取方法通过 **声明式验证模式组合（declarative validation schema composition）** 实现多阶段验证，以提取和处理嵌入的媒体交付平台元数据。其核心机制如下：

### 1. **多阶段验证管道**
验证模式按顺序组合成管道，每个阶段对前一阶段的输出进行验证和提取：
- **输入类型验证**：如 `str` 确保输入是字符串
- **解析转换**：如 `validate.parse_json()` 将字符串解析为 JSON 对象
- **结构验证**：如 `dict` 验证 JSON 对象结构
- **字段验证与提取**：如 `validate.get("key")` 提取特定字段

### 2. **组合操作符**
- **`validate.all()`**：按顺序验证多个 schema，每个 schema 的输出作为下一个 schema 的输入
- **`validate.any()`**：尝试多个 schema，返回第一个成功的结果
- **`validate.optional()`**：使字段验证可选，缺失时不报错
- **`validate.none_or_all()`**：如果输入为 `None` 则跳过验证，否则按 schema 验证
- **`validate.get()`**：从 dict 中提取指定键的值
- **`validate.union_get()`**：从 dict 中提取多个键的值

### 3. **典型实现流程**（以 okru.py 为例）
```python
schema_metadata = validate.Schema(
    validate.parse_html(),                    # 阶段 1: 解析 HTML
    validate.xml_find(".//*[@data-options]"), # 阶段 2: XPath 定位元素
    validate.get("data-options"),             # 阶段 3: 获取属性值
    validate.parse_json(),                    # 阶段 4: 解析 JSON
    {                                          # 阶段 5: 定义嵌套结构验证
        "author": validate.all(
            {validate.optional("name"): str}, # 验证 author.name 结构
            validate.get("name")              # 提取 name 值
        ),
        "movie": validate.all(
            {...},                             # 验证 movie 结构
            validate.union_get("id", "title") # 提取 id 和 title
        ),
        "hlsManifestUrl": validate.url(),     # 验证 HLS URL
        "videos": [...],                      # 验证视频列表
    },

```

### 4. **错误处理**
- 验证失败时抛出 `ValidationError`，包装在 `PluginError` 中
- 使用 `validate.optional()` 和 `validate.none_or_all()` 处理可选字段
- 错误消息包含验证失败的具体位置和原因

### 5. **关键特性**
- **声明式而非程序式**：避免手动错误处理
- **管道式处理**：数据流经多个验证阶段
- **类型安全**：每个阶段验证特定类型
- **嵌套支持**：可处理多层嵌套的 JSON 结构
- **URL 验证**：使用 `validate.url()` 及其子验证器（如 `validate.endswith()`）

这种设计使得插件实现者可以清晰地定义数据提取规则，同时获得有意义的错误消息，无需手动处理解析和验证逻辑。

L6: Introduction

L10: validation schemas which are used to verify and extract data from various inputs, for example HTTP responses.
L11:

L13: stream URLs, stream metadata and more from websites and web APIs.
L14: 
L15: Instead of verifying and extracting data programatically and having to perform error handling manually,
L16: declarative validation schemas allow defining comprehensive validation and extraction rules which are easy to understand

L18: 
L19: .. admonition:: Public interface
L20:    :class: caution
L21: 
L22:    While the internals are implemented in the ``streamlink.validate`` package,
L23:    :ref:`streamlink.plugin.api.validate <api/validate:Validation schemas>` provides the main public interface
L24:    for plugin implementors.
L25: 
L26: 
L27: Examples
L28: --------
L29: 
L30: Simple schemas
L31: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L32: 
L33: Let's begin with a few simple validation schemas which are not particularly useful yet.
L34: 
L35: .. code-block:: pycon
L36: 
L37:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

L39:     >>> schema_one = validate.Schema("123")
L40:     >>> schema_two = validate.Schema(123)
L41:     >>> schema_three = validate.Schema(int, 123.0)

L43:     >>> schema_one.validate("123")

L45:     >>> schema_two.validate(123)
L46:     123
L47:     >>> schema_three.validate(123)
L48:     123

L50: First, three :class:`Schema` instances are created, ``schema_one``, ``schema_two`` and ``schema_three``.
L51: 
L52: The :class:`Schema` class is the main schema validation interface and the outer wrapper for all schema definitions.
L53: It is a subclass of :class:`validate.all <all>` which additionally implements the :meth:`Schema.validate()` method.
L54: This interface is expected by various Streamlink methods and functions when passing the ``schema`` argument/keyword,
L55: for example to the :class:`HTTPSession <streamlink.session.Streamlink.http>` methods or :mod:`streamlink.utils.parse` functions.
L56: 
L57: The :class:`validate.all <all>` class takes a sequence of schema object arguments and validates each one in order.
L58: All schema objects in this schema container must be valid.
L59: 
L60: Schema objects can be anything, and depending on their type, different validations will be applied. In our example, both
L61: ``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``"123"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas
L62: ``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate
L63: only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.
L64: 
L65: As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't
L66: much interesting in this example.

L68: The ``"123"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for
L69: all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,
L70: and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object
L71: and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.
L72: ``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.
L73: This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected
L74: when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,
L75: the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole
L76: ``schema_three`` to be ``123``.

L80: .. code-block:: pycon
L81: 
L82:     >>> schema_one.validate(123)
L83:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):
L84:       123 does not equal '123'
L85: 
L86:     >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)
L87:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):
L88:       Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float

L90: The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``"123"``, so

L92: the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in
L93: a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.

L95: The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for

L100: Extracting JSON data
L101: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L102: 
L103: The next example shows how to read an optional integer value from JSON data.
L104: 
L105: .. code-block:: pycon
L106: 
L107:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
L108: 
L109:     >>> json_schema = validate.Schema(
L110:     ...     str,
L111:     ...     validate.parse_json(),
L112:     ...     {
L113:     ...         "status": validate.any(None, int),
L114:     ...     },
L115:     ...     validate.get("status"),
L116:     ... )
L117: 
L118:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":null}""")
L119:     None
L120:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":123}""")
L121:     123
L122: 
L123:     >>> json_schema.validate("""Not JSON""")
L124:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError:
L125:       Unable to parse JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ('Not JSON')
L126: 
L127:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":"unknown"}""")
L128:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(dict):
L129:       Unable to validate value of key 'status'
L130:       Context(AnySchema):
L131:         ValidationError(equality):
L132:           'unknown' does not equal None
L133:         ValidationError(type):
L134:           Type of 'unknown' should be int, but is str
L135: 
L136: Once again, we start with a new :class:`Schema` object which gets assigned to ``json_schema``. This schema collection validates
L137: four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.
L138: 
L139: Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set
L140: ``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.
L141: 
L142: Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns
L143: a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns
L144: something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input
L145: is indeed valid JSON data.
L146: 
L147: Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema
L148: be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which
L149: must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.
L150: For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is
L151: a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.
L152: 
L153: Here, the ``"status"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to
L154: :class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.
L155: Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema
L156: that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be
L157: ``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.
L158: 
L159: If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated
L160: by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.
L161: 
L162: The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.
L163: This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.
L164: And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``"status"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.
L165: The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using
L166: the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` schemas, but this isn't relevant here.

L168: Finding stream URLs in HTML
L169: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L170: 
L171: Let's imagine a simple website where a stream URL is embedded as JSON data in a ``data-player`` attribute of an unknown
L172: HTML element where the web player of that website reads from.
L173: 
L174: Extracting this data could be done by using regular expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,
L175: as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing
L176: a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.
L177: 
L178: Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query
L179: for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.

L181: We also don't want to raise validation errors unnecessarily when the user inputs a URL where no video player was found,

## 答案

Streamlink 的流获取方法通过 **声明式验证模式组合（declarative validation schema composition）** 实现多阶段验证，以提取和处理嵌入的媒体交付平台元数据。其核心机制如下：

### 1. **多阶段验证管道**
验证模式按顺序组合成管道，每个阶段对前一阶段的输出进行验证和提取：
- **输入类型验证**：如 `str` 确保输入是字符串
- **解析转换**：如 `validate.parse_json()` 将字符串解析为 JSON 对象
- **结构验证**：如 `dict` 验证 JSON 对象结构
- **字段验证与提取**：如 `validate.get("key")` 提取特定字段

### 2. **组合操作符**
- **`validate.all()`**：按顺序验证多个 schema，每个 schema 的输出作为下一个 schema 的输入
- **`validate.any()`**：尝试多个 schema，返回第一个成功的结果
- **`validate.optional()`**：使字段验证可选，缺失时不报错
- **`validate.none_or_all()`**：如果输入为 `None` 则跳过验证，否则按 schema 验证
- **`validate.get()`**：从 dict 中提取指定键的值
- **`validate.union_get()`**：从 dict 中提取多个键的值

### 3. **典型实现流程**（以 okru.py 为例）
```python
schema_metadata = validate.Schema(
    validate.parse_html(),                    # 阶段 1: 解析 HTML
    validate.xml_find(".//*[@data-options]"), # 阶段 2: XPath 定位元素
    validate.get("data-options"),             # 阶段 3: 获取属性值
    validate.parse_json(),                    # 阶段 4: 解析 JSON
    {                                          # 阶段 5: 定义嵌套结构验证
        "author": validate.all(
            {validate.optional("name"): str}, # 验证 author.name 结构
            validate.get("name")              # 提取 name 值
        ),
        "movie": validate.all(
            {...},                             # 验证 movie 结构
            validate.union_get("id", "title") # 提取 id 和 title
        ),
        "hlsManifestUrl": validate.url(),     # 验证 HLS URL
        "videos": [...],                      # 验证视频列表
    },
)
```

### 4. **错误处理**
- 验证失败时抛出 `ValidationError`，包装在 `PluginError` 中
- 使用 `validate.optional()` 和 `validate.none_or_all()` 处理可选字段
- 错误消息包含验证失败的具体位置和原因

### 5. **关键特性**
- **声明式而非程序式**：避免手动错误处理
- **管道式处理**：数据流经多个验证阶段
- **类型安全**：每个阶段验证特定类型
- **嵌套支持**：可处理多层嵌套的 JSON 结构
- **URL 验证**：使用 `validate.url()` 及其子验证器（如 `validate.endswith()`）

这种设计使得插件实现者可以清晰地定义数据提取规则，同时获得有意义的错误消息，无需手动处理解析和验证逻辑。", "source": "completed_sdk_research", "is_evidence": false, "independently_verified": false, "original_bytes": 2972, "kept_bytes": 2972, "truncated": false}}

How does the stream retrieval method implement multi-stage validation schema composition for extracting and processing embedded media delivery platform metadata?", "context": [{"path": "docs/api_guide/validate.rst", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 300, "content": "L1: Validation schemas
L2: ==================
L3: 
L4: .. currentmodule:: streamlink.plugin.api.validate
L5: 
L6: Introduction
L7: ------------
L8: 
L9: The :ref:`streamlink.plugin.api.validate <api/validate:Validation schemas>` module provides an API for defining declarative
L10: validation schemas which are used to verify and extract data from various inputs, for example HTTP responses.
L11: 
L12: Validation schemas are a powerful tool for :ref:`plugin <api/plugin:Plugin>` implementors to find and extract data like
L13: stream URLs, stream metadata and more from websites and web APIs.
L14: 
L15: Instead of verifying and extracting data programatically and having to perform error handling manually,
L16: declarative validation schemas allow defining comprehensive validation and extraction rules which are easy to understand
L17: and which raise errors with meaningful messages upon extraction failure.
L18: 
L19: .. admonition:: Public interface
L20:    :class: caution
L21: 
L22:    While the internals are implemented in the ``streamlink.validate`` package,
L23:    :ref:`streamlink.plugin.api.validate <api/validate:Validation schemas>` provides the main public interface
L24:    for plugin implementors.
L25: 
L26: 
L27: Examples
L28: --------
L29: 
L30: Simple schemas
L31: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L32: 
L33: Let's begin with a few simple validation schemas which are not particularly useful yet.
L34: 
L35: .. code-block:: pycon
L36: 
L37:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
L38: 
L39:     >>> schema_one = validate.Schema("123")
L40:     >>> schema_two = validate.Schema(123)
L41:     >>> schema_three = validate.Schema(int, 123.0)
L42: 
L43:     >>> schema_one.validate("123")
L44:     '123'
L45:     >>> schema_two.validate(123)
L46:     123
L47:     >>> schema_three.validate(123)
L48:     123
L49: 
L50: First, three :class:`Schema` instances are created, ``schema_one``, ``schema_two`` and ``schema_three``.
L51: 
L52: The :class:`Schema` class is the main schema validation interface and the outer wrapper for all schema definitions.
L53: It is a subclass of :class:`validate.all <all>` which additionally implements the :meth:`Schema.validate()` method.
L54: This interface is expected by various Streamlink methods and functions when passing the ``schema`` argument/keyword,
L55: for example to the :class:`HTTPSession <streamlink.session.Streamlink.http>` methods or :mod:`streamlink.utils.parse` functions.
L56: 
L57: The :class:`validate.all <all>` class takes a sequence of schema object arguments and validates each one in order.
L58: All schema objects in this schema container must be valid.
L59: 
L60: Schema objects can be anything, and depending on their type, different validations will be applied. In our example, both
L61: ``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``"123"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas
L62: ``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate
L63: only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.
L64: 
L65: As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't
L66: much interesting in this example.
L67: 
L68: The ``"123"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for
L69: all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,
L70: and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object
L71: and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.
L72: ``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.
L73: This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected
L74: when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,
L75: the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole
L76: ``schema_three`` to be ``123``.
L77: 
L78: Now let's have a look at validation errors.
L79: 
L80: .. code-block:: pycon
L81: 
L82:     >>> schema_one.validate(123)
L83:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):
L84:       123 does not equal '123'
L85: 
L86:     >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)
L87:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):
L88:       Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float
L89: 
L90: The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``"123"``, so
L91: a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>` is raised because the input value is not equal to
L92: the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in
L93: a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.
L94: 
L95: The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for
L96: the type ``int``, and despite the following schema being ``123.0``, which is a ``float`` object that would obviously validate
L97: a ``123.0`` ``float`` input when comparing equality, a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`
L98: is raised.
L99: 
L100: Extracting JSON data
L101: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L102: 
L103: The next example shows how to read an optional integer value from JSON data.
L104: 
L105: .. code-block:: pycon
L106: 
L107:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
L108: 
L109:     >>> json_schema = validate.Schema(
L110:     ...     str,
L111:     ...     validate.parse_json(),
L112:     ...     {
L113:     ...         "status": validate.any(None, int),
L114:     ...     },
L115:     ...     validate.get("status"),
L116:     ... )
L117: 
L118:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":null}""")
L119:     None
L120:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":123}""")
L121:     123
L122: 
L123:     >>> json_schema.validate("""Not JSON""")
L124:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError:
L125:       Unable to parse JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ('Not JSON')
L126: 
L127:     >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":"unknown"}""")
L128:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(dict):
L129:       Unable to validate value of key 'status'
L130:       Context(AnySchema):
L131:         ValidationError(equality):
L132:           'unknown' does not equal None
L133:         ValidationError(type):
L134:           Type of 'unknown' should be int, but is str
L135: 
L136: Once again, we start with a new :class:`Schema` object which gets assigned to ``json_schema``. This schema collection validates
L137: four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.
L138: 
L139: Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set
L140: ``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.
L141: 
L142: Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns
L143: a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns
L144: something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input
L145: is indeed valid JSON data.
L146: 
L147: Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema
L148: be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which
L149: must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.
L150: For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is
L151: a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.
L152: 
L153: Here, the ``"status"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to
L154: :class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.
L155: Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema
L156: that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be
L157: ``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.
L158: 
L159: If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated
L160: by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.
L161: 
L162: The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.
L163: This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.
L164: And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``"status"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.
L165: The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using
L166: the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` schemas, but this isn't relevant here.
L167: 
L168: Finding stream URLs in HTML
L169: ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
L170: 
L171: Let's imagine a simple website where a stream URL is embedded as JSON data in a ``data-player`` attribute of an unknown
L172: HTML element where the web player of that website reads from.
L173: 
L174: Extracting this data could be done by using regular expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,
L175: as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing
L176: a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.
L177: 
L178: Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query
L179: for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.
L180: 
L181: We also don't want to raise validation errors unnecessarily when the user inputs a URL where no video player was found,
L182: so we can instead return an empty list of streams in our plugin implementation and let Streamlink's CLI exit gracefully.
L183: Validation errors are only supposed to be raised when an actual error happened due to unexpected data,
L184: not when streams are offline or inaccessible.
L185: 
L186: Thanks to validation schemas, we can do all this declaratively without causing a mess when doing this programmatically.
L187: 
L188: .. code-block:: pycon
L189: 
L190:     >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
L191: 
L192:     >>> schema = validate.Schema(
L193:     ...     validate.parse_html(),
L194:     ...     validate.xml_xpath_string(".//*[@data-player][1]/@data-player"),
L195:     ...     validate.none_or_all(
L196:     ...         validate.parse_json(),
L197:     ...         {
L198:     ...             validate.optional("url"): validate.url(
L199:     ...                 path=validate.endswith(".m3u8"),
L200:     ...             ),
L201:     ...         },
L202:     ...         validate.get("url"),
L203:     ...     ),
L204:     ... )
L205: 
L206:     >>> schema.validate("""
L207:     ...     <!doctype html>
L208:     ...     <section class="no-video-player"></section>
L209:     ... """)
L210:     None
L211: 
L212:     >>> schema.validate("""
L213:     ...     <!doctype html>
L214:     ...     <section
L215:     ...         class="video-player"
L216:     ...         data-player="{
L217:     ...             "title":"Offline"
L218:     ...         }"
L219:     ...     >
L220:     ...         ...
L221:     ...     </section>
L222:     ... """)
L223:     None
L224: 
L225:     >>> schema.validate("""
L226:     ...     <!doctype html>
L227:     ...     <section
L228:     ...         class="video-player"
L229:     ...         data-player="{
L230:     ...             "title":"Live",
L231:     ...             "url":"https://host/hls-playlist.m3u8"
L232:     ...         }"
L233:     ...     >
L234:     ...         ...
L235:     ...     </section>
L236:     ... """)
L237:     'https://host/hls-playlist.m3u8'
L238: 
L239:     >>> schema.validate("""
L240:     ...     <!doctype html>
L241:     ...     <section
L242:     ...         class="video-player"
L243:     ...         data-player="{
L244:     ...             "title":"Live",
L245:     ...             "url":"https://host/dash-manifest.mpd"
L246:     ...         }"
L247:     ...     >
L248:     ...         ...
L249:     ...     </section>
L250:     ... """)
L251:     streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(NoneOrAllSchema):
L252:       ValidationError(dict):
L253:         Unable to validate value of key 'url'
L254:         Context(url):
L255:           Unable to validate URL attribute 'path'
L256:           Context(endswith):
L257:             '/dash-manifest.mpd' does not end with '.m3u8'
L258: 
L259: We start with a new :class:`Schema` and begin by parsing HTML using the :func:`validate.parse_html() <parse_html>`
L260: utility function. Similar to :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>`, it returns a :class:`validate.transform <transform>`
L261: schema. :func:`validate.parse_html() <parse_html>` however returns a parsed HTML node tree via Streamlink's
L262: :ref:`lxml dependency <install:Dependencies>`.

## 答案

Streamlink 的流获取方法通过 **声明式验证模式组合（declarative validation schema composition）** 实现多阶段验证，以提取和处理嵌入的媒体交付平台元数据。其核心机制如下：

### 1. **多阶段验证管道**
验证模式按顺序组合成管道，每个阶段对前一阶段的输出进行验证和提取：
- **输入类型验证**：如 `str` 确保输入是字符串
- **解析转换**：如 `validate.parse_json()` 将字符串解析为 JSON 对象
- **结构验证**：如 `dict` 验证 JSON 对象结构
- **字段验证与提取**：如 `validate.get("key")` 提取特定字段

### 2. **组合操作符**
- **`validate.all()`**：按顺序验证多个 schema，每个 schema 的输出作为下一个 schema 的输入
- **`validate.any()`**：尝试多个 schema，返回第一个成功的结果
- **`validate.optional()`**：使字段验证可选，缺失时不报错
- **`validate.none_or_all()`**：如果输入为 `None` 则跳过验证，否则按 schema 验证
- **`validate.get()`**：从 dict 中提取指定键的值
- **`validate.union_get()`**：从 dict 中提取多个键的值

### 3. **典型实现流程**（以 okru.py 为例）
```python
schema_metadata = validate.Schema(
    validate.parse_html(),                    # 阶段 1: 解析 HTML
    validate.xml_find(".//*[@data-options]"), # 阶段 2: XPath 定位元素
    validate.get("data-options"),             # 阶段 3: 获取属性值
    validate.parse_json(),                    # 阶段 4: 解析 JSON
    {                                          # 阶段 5: 定义嵌套结构验证
        "author": validate.all(
            {validate.optional("name"): str}, # 验证 author.name 结构
            validate.get("name")              # 提取 name 值
        ),
        "movie": validate.all(
            {...},                             # 验证 movie 结构
            validate.union_get("id", "title") # 提取 id 和 title
        ),
        "hlsManifestUrl": validate.url(),     # 验证 HLS URL
        "videos": [...],                      # 验证视频列表
    },
)
```

### 4. **错误处理**
- 验证失败时抛出 `ValidationError`，包装在 `PluginError` 中
- 使用 `validate.optional()` 和 `validate.none_or_all()` 处理可选字段
- 错误消息包含验证失败的具体位置和原因

### 5. **关键特性**
- **声明式而非程序式**：避免手动错误处理
- **管道式处理**：数据流经多个验证阶段
- **类型安全**：每个阶段验证特定类型
- **嵌套支持**：可处理多层嵌套的 JSON 结构
- **URL 验证**：使用 `validate.url()` 及其子验证器（如 `validate.endswith()`）

"""
$description Russian live-streaming and video hosting social platform.
$url ok.ru
$url mobile.ok.ru
$type live, vod
$metadata id
$metadata author
$metadata title
"""

import logging
import re
from urllib.parse import unquote

from streamlink.exceptions import NoStreamsError
from streamlink.plugin import Plugin, pluginmatcher
from streamlink.plugin.api import validate
from streamlink.stream.dash import DASHStream
from streamlink.stream.hls import HLSStream
from streamlink.stream.http import HTTPStream


log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@pluginmatcher(
    name="default",
    pattern=re.compile(r"https?://(?:www\.)?ok\.ru/"),
)
@pluginmatcher(
    name="mobile",
    pattern=re.compile(r"https?://m(?:obile)?\.ok\.ru/"),
)
class OKru(Plugin):
    QUALITY_WEIGHTS = {
        "full": 1080,
        "1080": 1080,
        "hd": 720,
        "720": 720,
        "sd": 480,
        "480": 480,
        "360": 360,
        "low": 360,
        "lowest": 240,
        "mobile": 144,
    }

    @classmethod
    def stream_weight(cls, key):
        weight = cls.QUALITY_WEIGHTS.get(key)
        if weight:
            return weight, "okru"

        return super().stream_weight(key)

    def _canonicalize_mobile_url(self):
        url = self.session.http.get(
            self.url,
            schema=validate.Schema(
                validate.parse_html(),
                validate.xml_xpath_string(".//head/link[@rel='canonical'][@href][1]/@href"),
                validate.none_or_all(
                    validate.url(),
                ),
            ),
        )
        if not url or not self.matchers["default"].pattern.match(url):
            raise NoStreamsError

        self.url = url

>>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> schema_one = validate.Schema("123")
    >>> schema_two = validate.Schema(123)
    >>> schema_three = validate.Schema(int, 123.0)

    >>> schema_one.validate("123")
    '123'
    >>> schema_two.validate(123)
    123
    >>> schema_three.validate(123)
    123

First, three :class:`Schema` instances are created, ``schema_one``, ``schema_two`` and ``schema_three``.

The :class:`Schema` class is the main schema validation interface and the outer wrapper for all schema definitions.
It is a subclass of :class:`validate.all <all>` which additionally implements the :meth:`Schema.validate()` method.
This interface is expected by various Streamlink methods and functions when passing the ``schema`` argument/keyword,
for example to the :class:`HTTPSession <streamlink.session.Streamlink.http>` methods or :mod:`streamlink.utils.parse` functions.

The :class:`validate.all <all>` class takes a sequence of schema object arguments and validates each one in order.
All schema objects in this schema container must be valid.

Schema objects can be anything, and depending on their type, different validations will be applied. In our example, both
``schema_one`` and ``schema_two`` contain only one schema object, namely ``"123"`` and ``123`` respectively, whereas
``schema_three`` contains two schema objects, ``int`` and ``123.0``. This means that the first two schemas validate
only one condition, while the third one validates two, first ``int``, then ``123.0``.

As you've probably already noticed, validation schemas also have a return value for their extraction purpose, but this isn't
much interesting in this example.

The ``"123"``, ``123`` and ``123.0`` schemas are simple :func:`equality validations <validate>`. This is the case for
all basic objects, and all they do is validate and return the input value again. ``int`` however is a ``type`` object,
and thus a :func:`type validation <_validate_type>`, which checks whether the input is an instance of the schema object
and then also returns the input value again. Since ``123`` is an ``int``, the schema is valid for that input.
``schema_three`` however hasn't finished validating yet at this point, as it defines two validation schemas in total.
This means that the return value of the ``int`` validation gets passed to the ``123.0`` schema validation, and as expected
when checking ``123 == 123.0``, despite both the input and schema being different types, namely ``int`` and ``float``,
the validation succeeds and returns its input value again, causing the return value of the whole
``schema_three`` to be ``123``.

Now let's have a look at validation errors.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> schema_one.validate(123)
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(equality):
      123 does not equal '123'

    >>> schema_three.validate(123.0)
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(type):
      Type of 123.0 should be int, but is float

The first :meth:`Schema.validate()` call passes ``123`` to ``schema_one``. ``schema_one`` however expects ``"123"``, so
a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>` is raised because the input value is not equal to
the schema. :meth:`Schema.validate()` catches the error and wraps it in
a :class:`PluginError <streamlink.exceptions.PluginError>` with a specific validation message.

The second validation also fails, but here, it's because of the input type. The first sub-schema explicitly checks for
the type ``int``, and despite the following schema being ``123.0``, which is a ``float`` object that would obviously validate
a ``123.0`` ``float`` input when comparing equality, a :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`
is raised.

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The next example shows how to read an optional integer value from JSON data.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> json_schema = validate.Schema(
    ...     str,
    ...     validate.parse_json(),
    ...     {
    ...         "status": validate.any(None, int),
    ...     },
    ...     validate.get("status"),
    ... )

    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":null}""")
    None
    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":123}""")
    123

    >>> json_schema.validate("""Not JSON""")
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError:
      Unable to parse JSON: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) ('Not JSON')

    >>> json_schema.validate("""{"status":"unknown"}""")
    streamlink.exceptions.PluginError: Unable to validate result: ValidationError(dict):
      Unable to validate value of key 'status'
      Context(AnySchema):
        ValidationError(equality):
          'unknown' does not equal None
        ValidationError(type):
          Type of 'unknown' should be int, but is str

Once again, we start with a new :class:`Schema` object which gets assigned to ``json_schema``. This schema collection validates
four schemas in total. Each of them must be valid, with each output being the input of the next one.

Since our goal is to parse JSON data and extract data from it, this means that we should only accept string inputs, so we set
``str`` as the first schema in this :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection.

Next is the :func:`validate.parse_json() <parse_json>` validation, a call of a utility function which returns
a :class:`validate.transform <transform>` schema object that does exactly what its name suggests: it takes an input and returns
something else. In this case, obviously, strings are the input and a parsed JSON object is the output, assuming that the input
is indeed valid JSON data.

Now we validate the parsed JSON object. We expect the JSON data to be a JSON ``object``, so we let the next validation schema
be a :func:`dict validation <_validate_dict>`. :class:`dict` validation schemas define a set of key-value pairs which
must exist in the input, unless keys are set as optional using :class:`validate.optional <optional>`.
For the sake of simplicity, this isn't the case in this example just yet. Each value of the key-value pairs is
a validation schema on its own where the input is validated against.

Here, the ``"status"`` key has a :class:`validate.any <any>` validation schema, which is also a schema collection, similar to
:class:`validate.all <all>`, but :class:`validate.any <any>` requires at least one sub-schema to be valid, not all.
Each sub-schema receives the same input, and the output of the overall schema collection is the output of the first sub-schema
that's valid. For our example, this means that the value of the ``status`` key in the JSON data must either be
``None`` (``null``) or an ``int``.

If any of the schemas in a nested schema definition like that fails, then a validation error stack will be generated
by :class:`ValidationError <streamlink.validate._exception.ValidationError>`, as shown above.

The last of the four schemas in the outer :class:`validate.all <all>` schema collection is a :class:`validate.get <get>` schema.
This schema works on any kind of input which implements :func:`__getitem__()`, for example :class:`dict` objects.
And as expected, it attempts to get and return the ``"status"`` key of the output of the previous :class:`dict` validation.
The :mod:`validation <streamlink.plugin.api.validate>` module also supports getting multiple values at once using
the :class:`validate.union <union>` or :class:`validate.union_get <union_get>` schemas, but this isn't relevant here.

Finding stream URLs in HTML
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Let's imagine a simple website where a stream URL is embedded as JSON data in a ``data-player`` attribute of an unknown
HTML element where the web player of that website reads from.

Extracting this data could be done by using regular expressions, but then we'd have to take HTML syntax into account,
as well as JSON syntax which should usually be HTML-encoded in that HTML element attribute, which would make writing
a regular expression even harder, apart from the fact that the JSON data structure could easily change at any time.

Therefore it would make much more sense parsing the HTML data, querying the resulting node tree using an XPath query
for getting the attribute value, then parsing the JSON data and finally finding and validating the stream URL.

We also don't want to raise validation errors unnecessarily when the user inputs a URL where no video player was found,
so we can instead return an empty list of streams in our plugin implementation and let Streamlink's CLI exit gracefully.
Validation errors are only supposed to be raised when an actual error happened due to unexpected data,
not when streams are offline or inaccessible.

Thanks to validation schemas, we can do all this declaratively without causing a mess when doing this programmatically.

.. code-block:: pycon

    >>> from streamlink.plugin.api import validate

    >>> schema = validate.Schema(
    ...     validate.parse_html(),
    ...     validate.xml_xpath_string(".//*[@data-player][1]/@data-player"),
    ...     validate.none_or_all(
    ...         validate.parse_json(),
    ...         {
    ...             validate.optional("url"): validate.url(
    ...                 path=validate.endswith(".m3u8"),
    ...             ),

    ...     >
